items.t: Applauded the announcement that Ohio was named number one in the nation for business in CNBC's America's Top States for Business rankings.
items.q: Speaker of the Ohio House Matt Huffman (R–Lima) today applauded the announcement that the State of Ohio has been named number one in the nation for business, according to CNBC America’s Top States for Business rankings.

items.t: Worked to make the state budget prioritize taxpayers.
items.q: Throughout his career, Speaker-elect Huffman has worked to make sure the budget prioritizes taxpayers with the idea that it’s not the government’s money, it's their money.

record.t: Was scheduled to lead the ceremony in the Senate at the first session of the 136th General Assembly, when Rob McColley took the oath as Senate President.
record.q: On January 6, 2025, Senate President Matt Huffman will lead the ceremony during the first session of the 136th General Assembly in the Senate as incoming President Rob McColley takes the oath of office for the Upper Chamber.

record.t: Served as Senate President since January 2021.
record.q: Huffman has served as Senate President since January of 2021.

record.t: Began serving in the Ohio House of Representatives (2007).
record.q: In 2007, he began his service in the Ohio House of Representatives.

record.t: Was unanimously elected by the House Republican Caucus to become Speaker of the Ohio House.
record.q: The House Republican Caucus unanimously elected Senator Huffman during a meeting of its members Wednesday night.

record.t: Served as Speaker Pro-Tempore under Speaker William "Batch" Batchelder.
record.q: Huffman, a Lima Republican, served as Speaker Pro-Tempore under the late and legendary Speaker of the House William “Batch” Batchelder.

record.t: Was elected to Lima City Council and later became City Council President.
record.q: He was elected to Lima City Council and later became City Council President.

record.t: Welcomed Ohio's electors to the Electoral College meeting in the Senate Chamber.
record.q: This week, Huffman also welcomed Ohio’s electors to the 56th Electoral College in the Senate Chamber certifying Donald Trump and Ohio’s U.S. Senator J.D. Vance as the winners of the presidential race in Ohio.

record.t: Joined a House Veterans and Military Development Committee tour and meeting at the Lima Army Tank Plant.
record.q: Richardson and members of the committee were joined by Speaker Matt Huffman (R-Lima) for the tour and committee meeting.
